body:
## Summary

Four methods fail when the trial-status column does not have the name `S`. These methods are `ec_ipw()`, `ec_aipw()`, `did_ec_ipw()`, and `did_ec_aipw()`. If an object with the same name is in the user's R session, the method uses that object instead. This gives an incorrect result without a message.

## Steps to reproduce

```r
library(rdborrow)
d <- SyntheticData
names(d)[names(d) == "S"] <- "in_trial"

method <- ec_ipw(ps_formula = "in_trial ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5")
analysis <- setup_analysis_primary(
  data = d,
  trial_status_col_name = "in_trial",
  treatment_col_name = "A",
  outcome_col_name = c("y1", "y2"),
  covariates_col_name = c("x1", "x2", "x3", "x4", "x5"),
  method_weighting_obj = method
)
run_analysis(analysis)
```

## Expected result

The method uses the column `in_trial` and gives the same result as with a column named `S`.

## Actual result

```
Error in eval(predvars, data, env) : object 'in_trial' not found
```

`did_ec_ipw()` and `did_ec_aipw()` give the same error through `setup_analysis_OLE()`. `did_ec_or()` and `scm()` work.

## Cause

1. `.build_analysis_df()` copies the trial-status column into an internal column named `S`.
2. `estimate()` then changes the left side of `ps_formula` to the user's column name, `in_trial`.
3. The internal data does not contain `in_trial`. `glm()` cannot find it in the data, so it looks for an object with that name in the formula's environment.

The tests, vignettes, and examples all use the name `S`. Thus, no test found this problem.

## Correction

Change the left side of the formula to the internal name `S`, not to the user's column name:

```r
ps_formula <- sub("^[^~]*~", "S ~", method@ps_formula)
```

Make the same change for `trt_formula` in the DID methods. That formula uses the internal name `A`.

Add a test that uses a trial-status column and a treatment column with different names.

## Affected functions

| Function | Location |
|---|---|
| `ec_ipw()` | `R/ec_ipw.R:96` |
| `ec_aipw()` | `R/ec_aipw.R:117` |
| `did_ec_ipw()` | `R/did_ec_ipw.R:85`, `:88` (`trt_formula`) |
| `did_ec_aipw()` | `R/did_ec_aipw.R:99`, `:102` (`trt_formula`) |

## Related

Found by all four testers in the adversarial review pilot (#101). Related to #83.
title: Methods with a participation formula fail when the trial-status column is not named S
